question: What follows if knowability were treated as a property of objects?
premises: If knowability were an object's property, objects would remain unknowable even when described in knowledge.
A pot may have features like a broad base.
The mere presence of such features does not make another thing share them.
inference: Treating knowability as an object-property fails to explain how objects become known.
plain_english: If knowability were a property of objects, they would remain unknowable even when described in knowledge. Just as a pot may have a broad base and other features, that alone does not make something else take on those features.
